 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the insurance company seeking to set aside the judgment and award dated 28.12.2022 passed by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and JMFC & MACT, Raichur.
2. Heard on admission.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that the lorry insured by the appellant was not involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the said lorry.

The tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence produced by the appellant and passed the impugned judgment holding that the appellant and the insured-owner of the lorry are liable to pay the compensation.

Further it is submitted that tribunal did not consider the defence taken up by the appellant that owner/insured of the vehicle used the vehicle without a valid permit and allowed the vehicle to be driven by a person not holding valid DL in violation of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Further the tribunal has failed to appreciate the facts on record.
The tribunal has not considered the defence taken by the appellant.
On all these grounds sought for allowing this appeal.
4. A perusal of the impugned judgment it is crystal clear that to prove the case of the claimants/petitioners, 3 witnesses are examined as PW1 to PW3.
14 documents got marked as Exs.P-1 to P-14.
After thorough investigation the IO has submitted the charge sheet as per Ex.P-3 against the driver of the lorry.
Ex.P-6 is the certified copy of the order sheet of CC No.52/2020.
The respondent No.1 has pleaded guilty for the alleged commission of offences and has also paid the fine amount.

5. Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in proper and perspective manner and has given finding to the effect that accident occurred due to rash and negligent manner on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA-36-5939.
The tribunal has discussed as to the liability of the insurance company.

In para 20 to 22 the tribunal has observed as under:
"20 Liability: Leamed counsel for respondent No.3 has argued by referring evidence of RW.1 doctor and Ex.R.1 and 2 MLC and intimation issued to SHO Lingasugur Government Hospital.
RW.1 has deposed that the petitioner has approached the hospital for treatment with history of sustaining injury in tractor and Motorcycle accident.
He has placed on record Ex.R.1 MLC which find reference about history of Bike and tractor involvement in the accident.
Whereas PW.1 has denied the disclosure of history of accident to the said doctor.
It is elicited during the cross- examination of PW.1 that he has not stated about the vehicles involved in the accident before doctor.

It is noticed that there is variation of time of accident The Branch Manager National Insurance ... vs Ramalingappa S/O Ramanna Madar And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124219199/

sentences.text: In this background I have gone through charge sheet material.
The investigation officer has filed charge-sheet stating that the accident occurred due to the negligent act on the part of driver of lorry have disputed the said fact seriously.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.1 and 2 are the residence of Honnalli village.
Whereas the petitioner is resident of Gudadanal village.
There is nothing on record to show that respondent No.1 and 2 either relatives or known to the petitioner so as to hold that they colluded with him.
In the absence of such evidence it cannot be readily accepted that the entire investigation is at the mercy of petitioner.
Furthermore, respondent No.1 has admitted his guilt before the court which is manifest from Ex.P.6.

In view of above referred material evidence just because RW.1 has recorded the history of accident between bike and tractor cannot be made base to over through the entire charge-sheet material and evidence of PW.1 and 2.
22.
The petitioner has placed on record Driving license of Respondent No.I at Ex.P.13.
The offending lorry was insured with respondent No.3 which is evident from Ex R.4.
In view of the same respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.3 being the insurer of offending Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 36/5939 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in affirmative."
6. On perusal of these materials, I do not find any material to interfere with the impugned judgment and award.
Hence, appeal is dismissed.
